newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury says Lehman violated auction rules.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury says Lehman violated auction rules.

text.p: The Treasury Department said on Thursday that New York securities dealer Lehman Brothers acknowledged unintentionally violating its reporting rules for participating in government auctions last year.

But Treasury said it was not imposing any penalties because it found no evidence that Lehman was attempting to manipulate market prices. Treasury said it was satisfied with corrective measures Lehman has taken voluntarily.

Treasury released copies of letters in which Lehman said that clerical errors were to blame for 13 instances in which Lehman misreported its net long position on certain securities during a six-month period that ended May 31, 1995.
But Treasury said in a letter to Lehman that the reporting errors "appear to have resulted from mistakes attributable to improperly trained staff and inadequate internal operating procedures."
It added, "Treasury does not anticipate taking any further actions with regard to the reporting violations discussed in your letter."
